The ETES shall consist of a recuperated sCO Brayton cycle 2 using 2-tank indirect thermal energy storage and an electric heater for heat input. The salt slurry uses chloride salt and operates at a maximum temperature of 500-720°C. The ETES uses dry air cooling. The salt slurry will be modeled as a sensible heat storage medium and as a latent heat storage medium. NLR will use the model to do parametric analysis of the factors affecting the performance (ex., round trip efficiency) of the ETES system. NLR will work with PowderMet to estimate the costs of system components and total system costs, with the levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) as the primary cost metric. CRADA benefit to DOE, Participant, and U.S.Taxpayer: • Assists laboratory in achieving programmatic scope • Enhances the laboratory’s core competencies Summary of Research Results: • Task 1: NREL will develop recuperated sCO2 Brayton power cycle model and generate • reduced-order model for input to SAM. (+2 weeks from project start date) • Task 2: NREL will develop thermal energy storage (TES) and heat exchange subsystem models using the PowderMet salt slurry assuming sensible heat storage. (+4 weeks from project start date) using thermodynamic data for the slurry provided by Powdermet. • Task 3: NREL will customize the dispatch and TES controllers in SAM to work with the ETES model (+6 weeks from the project start date). • Task 4: NREL with assistance from PowderMet, will develop rough cost estimates for ETES components and total system on sizing system and cost estimates. (+8 weeks from project start date). • Task 5: NREL will perform sensitivity analysis on ETES model to determine key factors and parameters affecting system cost and performance (+10 weeks from project start date). • Task 6: NREL will develop thermal energy storage (TES) and heat exchange subsystem models using the PowderMet salt slurry assuming latent heat storage and perform sensitivity analysis similar to that in Task 5. This task may be cancelled if, in consultation with PowderMet, it is determined that latest heat thermal energy storage is not possible and/or advantageous. (+12 weeks from project start date). • Task 7: At the direction of PowderMet, NREL will explore alternative system designs, cost estimates, or performance assumptions, consistent with the scope and subject to the availability of funding.
